article.title: Why Revenue Growth Should Be Split into Price, Frequency, and Customer Effects
article.why: Learn to distinguish sustainable behavioral growth from price and population effects.

paragraphs.en:
When revenue grows by 10 percent, the result looks positive, but the headline number does not explain why it grew. Revenue can rise because prices increased, customers visited more often, customers bought more items per visit, or the business served more customers. These mechanisms have different implications for future growth.

A simple starting point is to think of revenue as the product of customer count, purchase frequency, and spending per purchase. Spending per purchase can then be separated further into the number of items and the average price paid. This decomposition turns one large number into several behavioral and economic drivers.

Suppose a supermarket reports 8 percent revenue growth. If customer count is unchanged and purchase frequency is also flat, but average basket value rises 8 percent, the next question is why baskets became more expensive. Customers may be buying more products, choosing premium products, or simply paying higher prices for the same goods. Inflation can therefore create nominal revenue growth without an equivalent increase in customer engagement.

The opposite pattern is also possible. Average basket value may remain flat while customer frequency rises. That can be strategically attractive because customers are choosing the store more often. Yet analysts should check whether the increase comes from the same customers or from a shift in customer mix. A promotion may temporarily increase visits while reducing margin.

Customer count requires similar care. More active customers can support growth, but the source matters. Are they genuinely new customers, reactivated customers, or existing customers newly captured by a changed identification rule? If membership definitions or data coverage changed, part of the apparent growth may be measurement rather than behavior.

For year-over-year reporting, analysts can build a bridge from last year’s revenue to this year’s revenue. One component represents customer-count change, another frequency change, another volume or basket change, and another price or mix effect. The exact formula depends on the business, but the purpose is consistent: explain which drivers produced the total movement.

Interactions complicate the arithmetic. If both customer count and frequency increase, assigning the combined effect to one driver requires a convention. Analysts should document the method rather than imply that decomposition is uniquely determined. Shapley-style allocation or sequential bridges can be useful when stakeholders need additive contributions.

The interpretation should also include margin. Revenue created by price increases or promotions may not translate into proportional profit. Higher frequency can be costly if incentives are expensive. Therefore, a good growth review connects revenue drivers with gross margin, retention, and customer value.

‘Revenue increased 10 percent’ is a result. ‘Revenue increased mainly because retained customers visited more frequently, while price contributed two points and customer count was stable’ is an explanation. The second statement gives decision-makers a much clearer view of what is working and whether the growth is likely to continue.
paragraphs.zh:
Revenue成長本身只是一個結果，必須拆成customer count、purchase frequency與spending per purchase，後者還可拆成購買量與價格。相同的8%成長，可能是更多顧客、更多來店、買更多商品，或只是價格上漲。這些原因對未來可持續性完全不同。

例如basket value上升若主要來自inflation，名目營收成長不代表engagement改善；frequency上升則可能代表顧客更常選擇該店，但也需確認是否由promotion暫時拉動。跨年可用revenue bridge拆出customer、frequency、volume、price/mix effect，並說明interaction的分配方法。最後還要連結margin、retention與customer value，避免把營收成長直接等同於商業品質改善。
paragraphs.ja:
Revenue成長はcustomer count、purchase frequency、spending per purchaseに分解できます。さらに一回当たり金額は数量とpriceに分けられます。同じ8％増でも、顧客数増、来店頻度増、購入量増、単なる値上げでは意味が異なります。

basket value上昇がinflation中心なら、名目売上は伸びてもengagementが改善したとは限りません。前年比較ではrevenue bridgeを作り、customer、frequency、volume、price/mix effectを説明すると有効です。interactionの配分方法も明記し、margin、retention、customer valueまで確認することで成長の質を判断できます。

business.term: We should separate price growth from behavioral growth before interpreting the result.
business.explanation: 區分價格因素與顧客行為因素。

sources: Retail revenue decomposition; price-volume-mix analysis; customer-frequency-basket frameworks.
